title: Multiplayer, Permissions, Remote Sync & Recording/Streaming Boundaries
start_authority: Owner Continue on 2026-08-27 America/Chicago after fresh verification of AIOC main b07b2bcabc383cc61a7febae0b4541f6f409e48e and application main 45752a7c1bad03b68b275638f4603ca33b8c2ea9, re-reading AAI-09 selection/program/backlog, AAI-08 completion, AAI-02 operation rights, AAI-03 remote-sync/streaming/export capabilities, the A5 authorization-before-projection seam and current execution-convergence controls.
objective: Implement and prove deterministic non-authoritative multiplayer audio permission/synchronization and capture-boundary decisions over completed AAI-01..08 and canonical A5 authorization evidence, without creating gameplay/permission truth, performing remote transport or recording/streaming media, or widening provider rights.

canonical_permission_authority.rule: AAI-09 consumes canonical subject/session/permission decision references from the existing A5 authorization-before-projection seam and Visibility/Permissions owner references. AAI-09 may validate and project audio presentation eligibility but cannot grant, revoke, infer or mutate campaign/gameplay/identity/session/permission authority.
canonical_permission_authority.hidden_data_rule: Protected/hidden records remain filtered by the canonical authorization layer before AAI-09. Audio denial must not reveal hidden target existence, counts, labels or reasons beyond safe nonblocking outcomes.

multiplayer_audio_permissions.rule: Hear, control and trigger eligibility are consumed as explicit canonical permission decisions tied to the current subject/session/permissionDecisionReference. Mismatched, missing or stale decision references fail closed. Audio availability never grants a capability and permission denial never blocks gameplay.

remote_sync.rule: AAI-09 produces deterministic presentation-only remote-sync intents and receipts. Stable syncId plus subject/session identity, monotonically increasing sequence and caller-owned previously-applied sync keys provide ordering/idempotency. Duplicate and stale messages are explicitly suppressed; reconnect/replay may re-evaluate only against current canonical permission evidence. AAI-09 owns no network transport and performs no provider or peer calls.

capture_boundaries.rule: Recording and streaming are separate presentation/capture intents, never consequences of playback. A capture intent requires explicit operation rights from AAI-02, compatible AAI-03 capability evidence when that capability exists, current canonical permission evidence and explicit participant-consent references for the requested scope. AAI-09 performs no media capture/transmission and no content-byte acquisition.
capture_boundaries.recording_rule: AAI-02 has an explicit record right but AAI-03 defines no recording capability key. Recording therefore fails closed as capability-unmodeled and cannot become capture-ready in AAI-09 without a separately governed capability extension.
capture_boundaries.streaming_rule: Streaming can become an intent-ready receipt only when AAI-02 stream rights are explicitly allowed, AAI-03 streaming capability negotiation is selectable, canonical permission evidence allows it and every required participant consent is explicitly granted. Intent-ready is not execution authority.
capture_boundaries.export_redistribution_rule: AAI-02 export and redistribute rights remain independent and are not implemented as AAI-09 capture operations. Stream/record permission never implies export or redistribution.

consent_privacy_security.rule: Consent is represented only by stable decision references, subject identity and scope/result; raw consent text, recordings, credentials, tokens and media bytes are excluded from deterministic receipts. Missing, denied, unknown or wrong-scope consent fails closed without disclosing unrelated participant state.

rights_and_provider_gates.rule: AAI-02 rights/provenance, AAI-03 capability, current provider terms/entitlement, AAI-05 semantic/runtime availability, AAI-06 provider restrictions, AAI-07 binding boundaries and AAI-08 preparation boundaries remain independent fail-closed gates. Provider linkage or playback success never implies remote-sync, record, stream, export or redistribution authority.

persistence.result: No new durable canonical AAI-09 persistence is required. Applied sync keys, last-seen sequences and consent/permission references are caller/session-owned ephemeral inputs; deterministic receipts are evidence/projection only.

validation_contract.focused: Prove canonical A5/Visibility permission-reference matching, safe denial, deterministic sync ordering/idempotency/stale suppression/reconnect re-evaluation, nonblocking unavailable audio, explicit record-vs-stream rights/capability/consent separation and zero gameplay/provider/capture execution.
validation_contract.predecessors: Run AAI-08 through AAI-01 verifiers plus MIB-11/D18 World-owner regression inside the AAI-09 profile; verify the A5 authorization-before-projection contract markers inside the AAI-09 invariant verifier.
validation_contract.workflow: Use the bounded current-tranche selector. AAI-09 adds exactly one governed Validation Core profile and no new workflow namespace or historical fanout.
validation_contract.final_gate: Exact candidate head must pass Repository Health, bounded AAI-09 self-hosted Linux and Windows Validation Core, deterministic cross-platform comparison and declared predecessor/owner regressions before merge.

preserved_boundaries: AAI-01..08 are completed_verified with no further implementation authority
AAI-09 authority is limited to deterministic multiplayer permission/sync/capture-boundary decisions on integration/aai-09-multiplayer-permissions-remote-sync-recording-streaming-boundaries
audio cannot grant/mutate canonical gameplay, identity, session or permission authority
remote sync is presentation intent only with no network/provider execution
recording capability remains unmodeled in AAI-03 and therefore fail-closed; streaming intent requires independent rights/capability/permission/consent evidence
